prompt: Which molecule has a bond angle of approximately 107°?
markscheme: **B.** Four domains with one lone pair: trigonal pyramidal, ~107°.

prompt: Which molecule is non-polar but contains polar bonds?
markscheme: **C.** The C–Cl dipoles cancel in the symmetrical tetrahedral molecule.

prompt: Which substance has the highest boiling point?
markscheme: **C.** NH₃ forms hydrogen bonds; the others have weaker intermolecular forces.

prompt: How many σ and π bonds are in hydrogen cyanide, H–C≡N?
markscheme: **A.** C–H is one σ; C≡N is one σ and two π.

prompt:
Consider the molecules BF₃ and NF₃.

**(a)** Draw the Lewis formula of each molecule. **[2]**

**(b)** Deduce the molecular geometry of each and estimate its bond angle. **[2]**

**(c)** Explain why NF₃ is polar but BF₃ is not. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** BF₃: B with three single bonds to F, three lone pairs on each F, no lone pair on B ✓; NF₃: N with three single bonds to F and one lone pair on N, three lone pairs on each F ✓

**(b)** BF₃ trigonal planar, 120° ✓; NF₃ trigonal pyramidal, ~107° (accept 100–108°) ✓

**(c)** Both have polar B–F/N–F bonds ✓; BF₃ is symmetrical so the bond dipoles cancel, whereas NF₃’s pyramidal shape (lone pair) means they do not cancel ✓

prompt:
**(a)** Draw two resonance structures for the ozone molecule, O₃. **[1]**

**(b)** Calculate the formal charge on each oxygen atom in one of your structures. **[2]**

**(c)** Predict, with a reason, how the two O–O bond lengths in ozone compare with the O–O single bond and the O=O double bond. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** O=O⁺–O⁻ and ⁻O–O⁺=O, central O with one lone pair ✓

**(b)** Double-bonded terminal O: $6 - 2 - 4 = 0$; central O: $6 - 3 - 2 = +1$ ✓; single-bonded terminal O: $6 - 1 - 6 = -1$ ✓

**(c)** Both bonds are equal in length ✓; intermediate between single and double because the π electrons are delocalised (bond order 1.5) ✓
